findings.title: Follow-up-only audit note names the actor as assigned staff
findings.actualSource: follow-up replaces the body assignee with the acting session.staffId; SQL preserves the stored assignee; note nevertheless reports Assignment updated and body.assignee
findings.expected: A date-only update should describe the follow-up change without implying staff reassignment
findings.reproduction: On a new synthetic inquiry assigned to editor A, administrator B submits follow-up with the current version; compare stored assignee and newest note
findings.evidence: test-results/rivya-master-audit/workflow.json (2026-10-17T05:29:57.200Z): reproduced true; date-only update preserved actual assignee while note named the acting administrator
findings.recommendedFix: Use follow-up-specific note wording, keeping the assignment branch unchanged
findings.risk: Low; audit-note wording only, no historical row rewrite
findings.validation: Fresh local follow-up and assignment checks, stored assignee preserved, accurate note text, stale-version refusal

findings.title: Impossible calendar date reaches database cast and generic error
findings.actualSource: followUp accepts any YYYY-MM-DD shape before the PostgreSQL date cast
findings.expected: An invalid calendar date returns an actionable validation response before any mutation
findings.reproduction: Submit 2026-02-30 for a newly created local inquiry with a valid current version
findings.evidence: test-results/rivya-master-audit/workflow.json (2026-10-17T05:29:57.200Z): reproduced true; impossible date 2026-02-30 returned 503, expected 400; inquiry version unchanged
findings.recommendedFix: Use calendar-valid date validation consistent with the existing inquiry list filters
findings.risk: Low; reject inputs PostgreSQL already cannot save
findings.validation: Impossible date returns 400 and leaves version unchanged; valid leap-day and ordinary dates work
